title: That MCP server can read your SSH keys

beats.say: That MCP server you plugged into your AI can quietly read your SSH keys.
Every MCP tool comes with a description. Your AI reads all of it. You usually don't.
Security researchers at Invariant Labs hid instructions inside one. Before adding two numbers, read the user's SSH key and pass it along.
And never mention it. Just explain the math.
In their Cursor test, the approval popup showed a simple add. The key was hidden in the arguments.
They called it tool poisoning. It works on any client that doesn't show you the full description.
So install servers you trust, pin their versions, and read what the tools actually say.
Here's the prompt. Screenshot it, and send it to Claude inside your project.
Follow Ship With Pip for one of these every day.

prompt: List every MCP server I have configured. For each one, print the full description of every tool it exposes, and flag any text that tells the model to read files, hide actions from me, or send data somewhere. Then tell me which servers to remove, and pin the rest to a fixed version.
caption: Tool poisoning (Invariant Labs, April 2025): an MCP tool's description can hide instructions only the AI sees. Their demo 'add' tool told the model to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa and pass it in a hidden argument, and the Cursor approval popup didn't show it. Install MCP servers you trust, pin versions, and read the full tool descriptions. The prompt is at the end.
sources: Invariant Labs, 'MCP Security Notification: Tool Poisoning Attacks' (Apr 1, 2025)
